subject: Post-call: Aurora Geo / Deployment requirements (hosted vs dedicated vs private) - recap & next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Hoffmann <lena.hoffmann@aurora-fin.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Aurora Geo / Deployment requirements (hosted vs dedicated vs private) - recap & next steps

Hi Lena — thanks again for the 30-minute call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the deployment and residency topics we discussed.

Summary of Aurora requirements we heard today:
- Primary requirement: all customer data for EU customers must remain in EU-controlled infrastructure; encryption keys managed by Aurora or a customer KMS is preferred.
- Secondary requirement: APAC expansion in 12–18 months — want to know whether Redwood Hosted can provide APAC-region endpoints or whether we should plan Dedicated / Private deployment for APAC.
- Peak latency target for customer-facing flows: <= 200ms 95p for text generation; embeddings tolerable up to 300ms.
- Compliance: SOC2 + ability to provide audit logs and data-retention controls.

Deployment options discussed (short):
- Hosted API (Redwood hosted): fastest to ship; we can pin to our EU region and restrict routing; good for initial POC if EU region is available in the account; uses Redwood-managed KMS unless Aurora requests customer KMS.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pool in EU region; gives stronger isolation and predictable throughput; supports customer KMS integration and longer log retention options.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full control, required if Aurora's procurement/legal says no managed-cloud in early phases; longer lead time and licensing.

Edge cases / routing notes: if Aurora wants Hosted now but APAC later, we can start with Hosted pinned to eu-central and later add APAC endpoints with cross-region routing policy (traffic regionalized, data-at-rest per-region). If strict data sovereignty is required (no cross-region replication for EU PII), Dedicated or Private may be needed.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical workshop (1-hour) with our Solutions Engineer to validate KMS options, network egress patterns, and how audit logs are captured (propose Wed 4/1 or Thu 4/2).
2) I’ll attach our DPA/Q questions and a one-pager comparing Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for EU/APAC scenarios. Please highlight any "deal-breaker" items.
3) If procurement needs pre-populated procurement language or an estimate for committed Dedicated capacity, Rafael (cc) will coordinate pricing.
4) We’ll prepare an APAC roadmap note (timing & options) after the tech workshop.

Attachments: Aurora-DPA-questions.pdf (questions for legal), redwood-deployment-options-1pager.pdf

If that all looks right I’ll schedule the workshop and loop in a SE.

Thanks — Camila
Camila Reyes

Thanks Camila — helpful summary. A few clarifications from my side: 
1) Customer KMS: Aurora would want tenant keys in a customer-controlled KMS for EU production data. Is that supported by Hosted, or would that require Dedicated?
2) APAC latency: our APAC customers are sensitive; can hosted EU endpoints be routed via APAC edge or would that create cross-border data flow we cannot allow?
3) Timeline: procurement is looking for a 60-day POC window from contract signature. Do you have a standard POC pricing / commitment model?

We’ll review the attached DPA questions and follow up with legal procurement on any redlines. Appreciate if you can confirm whether customer KMS + EU-only data residency is feasible on Hosted, or whether we should target Dedicated/Private out of the gate.

Best,
Lena

Hi Lena — thanks for the quick reply and the three clarifying questions. Short answers below; attached is a copyable DPA/Q we use for procurement. I’ll schedule the SE session once Rafael confirms pricing sketches.

1) Customer KMS on Hosted: we support BYOK for EU tenants via customer-managed KMS in supported cloud providers (AWS KMS in eu-west-1, Azure KeyVault in West Europe). Caveats: key import/export restrictions are subject to cloud provider policy; Hosted uses customer KMS for encryption-at-rest for model payloads and embeddings when configured, but some metadata (service logs) may reside in Redwood control plane unless you request full Private deployment. We will document exact log retention and export endpoints in the tech workshop.

2) APAC latency & routing: starting with Hosted EU endpoints will create cross-region traffic if APAC users call EU endpoints — that can violate data residency policies for PII. Options: (a) deploy Dedicated capacity in APAC region later and configure smart-routing so APAC traffic stays in-region, (b) use Hosted with regional endpoints (we have APAC regions in roadmap — ETA Q4 2026) or (c) Private/VPC deployed into your APAC infra. For a 12–18 month APAC plan, Dedicated as a follow-up is common.

3) POC timeline/pricing: we offer a 60-day POC model — Hosted metered with a token cap and a short Dedicated trial for predictable latency if you prefer. I’ll attach the POC worksheet and Rafael will share a simple Hosted vs Dedicated sketch.

Next steps (what I’ll do this week):
- Schedule 1-hour tech workshop (SE + Aditya) — propose Thu 4/1 10:00 CEST or Fri 4/2 14:00 SGT; will wait for your preference.
- Share Hosted BYOK doc and example KMS setup for eu-west-1 (Aditya to add details shortly).
- Rafael to send initial pricing sketches and procurement-ready language.

Attachments: Aurora-DPA-questions.pdf, redwood-deployment-options-1pager.pdf
Links: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/8473; SE onboarding doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Bxx-aurora-redwood

If that looks good, I’ll lock the workshop and include an agenda focused on KMS, audit logs, and sample latency numbers for EU-hosted vs Dedicated in eu-central.

Best — Camila
